title: Coder: a timed-out command whose process group isn't confirmed clear ends the turn as a stop nobody asked for
body:
Found while fixing #10248. Coder's last run of #10248 on coderos-4080 (task `ab924162549f`, codex gpt-6.1-sol, `~/coder-work-r.log`) ended with **"Coder stopped: the task was stopped, or its host refused to go on."** Nobody stopped it. The heredoc wasn't the cause either.

## What happened (read-only evidence from `~/.openagents/tasks`)

- Step 7's command was `cat >> crates/coder/src/task/owner/tests.rs <<'EOF' … EOF` followed by `cargo fmt --all; cargo test -p openagents-chat …; cargo test -p coder follower_ -- --test-threads=1 …`. The heredoc worked. The `openagents-chat` tests passed at about 180 s. Then `cargo test -p coder follower_` ran the agent's own new test. That test polls a follower until it ends, so it hung until the 300 s command deadline.
- Trace `ab924162549f….1.atif.jsonl`, effect 52 result: `"ending":"timed out","group_clear":false,"requested_stop":false,"seconds":300.36`.
- `crates/coder/src/task/adapter.rs` `Host::command`: `if !ended.group_clear { self.fail("supervised process cleanup is unknown"); }`. After that, `Host::cancelled()` is true, the microcoder loop ends `stopped` (`{"ending":{"reason":"stopped"},"steps":7}`), and the owner records `"ending":"cancelled_or_host_refusal","stop_requested":true,"group_clear":false`. The task (`task/ab92….json`) has only a `submit` command and no cancel command. It is left at `status: unknown`.
- The person reads the generic `cancelled_or_host_refusal` text from `coder_events::Mapper::end`. The real reason, a timed-out command whose processes the supervisor could not confirm gone, is dropped. `stop_requested: true` is recorded even though no stop was requested.

## Bugs

1. A command timeout whose process group isn't confirmed clear ends the whole turn, and the run is recorded as a stop the person asked for (`stop_requested: true`). The fault reason should be recorded as its own ending, for example `process_cleanup_unknown`, and not as a stop.
2. The person's message hides the reason. It should say that a command ran past its deadline and its processes could not be confirmed gone. The command should be named.
3. Possibly: why the group didn't clear. The test's children (owner fixtures that start supervised commands in their own process groups) likely outlived the kill. Decide whether a timed-out command's leftover descendants should end the turn at all, or be reaped or reported while the agent goes on.

Earlier Coder attempts on #10248 also did not start ("the workspace's source checkout cannot be found", "another process holds the task store lock"), so they never got this far.
